deck: Table Rock this morning: 910.46 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Streamer on the generate.
play.body: When SWPA spins it, Taneycomo becomes a small river. A dark wooly bugger in the seams.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: Table Rock held near 910.52 ft all week, a hair under full pool (915). Live USACE reading 11:00 CT: 910.52 ft, 20 cfs through the dam. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: At 910.46 ft the lake is showing significant bank and structure. Stumps, laydowns, and hazards in creek arms and coves sit closer to the surface — boat slowly and watch your electronics, especially in the James, Kings, and Long Creek arms.

Surface water has cooled into the upper 50s to low 60s with excellent clarity. Bass are holding on long points, gravel transitions into deeper water, and offshore brush in 25–45 feet. Clean presentations with jigs, drop-shots, and finesse rigs are key in this clear water. Mixed-bag action continues for walleye on points and crappie around deeper docks and brush.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~20 cfs at 11:00 CT (USACE live). Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: Cold bottom releases from Table Rock keep this tailwater in the mid-50s. Generation remains the complete tactic book: light early flows allow wading or light-line drifting with indicators. When turbines ramp (watch the afternoon 75–135 MW window on today's SWPA schedule), fish weighted rigs in the seams and current breaks.

From Table Rock Dam downstream to Fall Creek it is artificial lures and flies only — no soft plastics, no scented or natural baits. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, or other scented options for water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in the upper sections. Micro jigs, midges, scuds, and small streamers in natural colors are working well. Call 866-494-1993 for the live schedule so rising water does not catch you off guard.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
